Cleanup Ledger: Enbridge pipeline valve site in Hansen Township closes out with continuing obligations
what: Enbridge Energy's Jackson Road valve site closed Sept. 23 with a continuing obligation attached.
pitch: A pipeline company's contamination case at 6053 Jackson Rd closes, but the continuing obligation means something stays in the ground. Enbridge is a name readers know — worth explaining what's left behind and who's responsible.

name: Property transactions: $795,000 for buildings-only on a Town of Norrie road
what: 149 new Marathon County sales recorded, including a $795,000 Norrie single-family sale listed at zero acres.
pitch: A near-$800K price on a 'buildings/improvements only' record with 0.0 acres is unusual enough to be either a big rural estate or a data quirk. Either answer is a short story.

name: Coming Soon: two Stewart Avenue addresses still sending signals months after first permit
what: New arrivals on Sept. 23 refreshed pending signals at 2510 and 4611 Stewart Ave, Wausau.
pitch: A restaurant alteration permit at 2510 Stewart from July and an alcohol license extension at 4611 Stewart from June both got fresh activity. Two Stewart Ave openings in the pipeline — readers always want to know what's going in.

name: Gavel: County Board and Environmental Resources Committee both set for Nov. 24
what: Sixteen new meetings posted, including a Wausau Citizen Advisory Committee meeting Sept. 30.
pitch: Wednesday's Citizen Advisory Committee is the only near-term item and is worth staffing. The Nov. 24 Environmental Resources Committee is a natural place to raise the Enbridge closure once the BRRTS file is in hand.

name: Watch Ledger: 28 new ALPR cameras added, all in the Kenosha area
what: 28 camera records arrived, with sampled entries in Kenosha County, including one operated by Lowe's.
pitch: No Marathon County hook in the sample, so this is background not a story yet. But a private retailer listed as camera operator alongside Flock Safety is a thread worth pulling if the same pattern reaches Wausau.

name: Property transactions: 186 new Marathon County deeds land at once, with Wausau single-family sales near $310K
what: 186 new DOR sale records posted; total holdings re-set from 644 to 627.
pitch: The biggest single data drop in the brief. A batch this size is where repeat buyers, LLC purchases, municipal acquisitions and outlier prices hide — worth a sort before the week's news meeting.

name: Gavel: Wausau Finance and Common Council both meet Tuesday, Oct. 13
what: Eight meetings added, including Finance at 5:15 p.m. and Common Council at 6:30 p.m. Oct. 13.
pitch: Back-to-back finance and council on one night is the week's clearest staffing call. Check whether either agenda touches any address showing up in this week's 186 new property records.

name: Watch Ledger: roster drops 8 net even as 12 new Flock cameras appear
what: Twelve cameras added and roughly twenty dropped off; several new entries list no operator.
pitch: A net decline means cameras came down or stopped reporting — as newsworthy as new ones going up. Two of three sampled new cameras have null operator and null zone, meaning no agency is named.

name: Cleanup Ledger: two contamination case events, both outside Marathon County
what: Premier Auto Body in Marshfield closed; a new case opened at 2111 Jefferson St., Wisconsin Rapids.
pitch: Thin for a Marathon audience, but the Marshfield closure sits in WPR's coverage footprint. The Jefferson Rapids opening is brand new — what triggered it is the only question that matters.

name: Court tracker: Wausau man pleads not guilty in bail jumping, disorderly conduct case
what: Case 2026CM000231 in Marathon County moved to a not-guilty plea on Oct. 1.
pitch: A single misdemeanor plea is routine unless the defendant or the underlying case is recognizable. Worth two minutes to check the name before deciding it isn't a story.

name: Care Ledger: enforcement file and a follow-up visit at license 0008499
what: A March 2025 complaint survey at license 0008499 carried an enforcement document, followed by an August verification visit.
pitch: Most assisted-living surveys end with a statement of deficiencies only. This one drew a separate enforcement PDF and a return visit five months later — the state's escalation ladder, on a Marathon County license.

name: Care Ledger: archive jumps from 152 to 546 inspection records
what: The ledger more than tripled overnight, backfilling years of survey and complaint records for local licenses.
pitch: First time we can see repeat offenders instead of one-off inspections. Sort by license and count complaint/self-report surveys — the facilities with three or four are the story, not the ones with one.

name: Care Ledger: a complaint-surveyed license that's no longer on the state roster
what: License 0008655 shows a 2023 complaint/self-report survey and is now flagged as expired from the state list.
pitch: A facility that drew a complaint investigation and then dropped off the licensing roster. Did it close, sell, or surrender? Residents had to go somewhere — that's the human end of the story.

name: Property transactions: 131 deeds land at once, including LLC buys well under market
what: A batch of 131 early-October Marathon County sales posted, including a $58,895 Wausau house bought by an LLC.
pitch: Huddle Up Housing LLC paid under $59,000 for 822 Single Ave the same week a Chellis Street house went for $170,000. Worth checking how many of the 131 went to LLCs and whether any names repeat.

name: Gavel: December county committee calendar posts, including Public Safety
what: Seventeen meetings added, including a Dec. 8 Public Safety Committee and Dec. 10 Executive Committee.
pitch: Not this week's story, but Public Safety is the committee that touches sheriff's camera and ALPR decisions. Worth watching the agenda when it posts against the Watch Ledger's 2,117-camera roster.

name: Care Ledger: enforcement paperwork attached to a Marathon-area assisted living facility, with a follow-up verification visit
what: New record for facility 0008499 includes a March 2025 enforcement document plus an August verification visit.
pitch: Most Care Ledger entries are statements of deficiency alone. This one carries an enforcement document and a return visit — meaning the state thought the problem was serious enough to check whether it got fixed.

name: Gavel: Wausau Finance Committee meets twice in eight days
what: Fifteen meetings added, including Wausau Finance Committee on Oct. 20 and Oct. 27.
pitch: Two finance meetings inside a week usually means budget season crunch or something that couldn't wait. Worth seeing which it is before the council votes on anything with a dollar figure attached.

name: Cleanup Ledger: four DOT bridge contamination cases closed in Cleveland and Seneca towns
what: Four new events, all closures of WisDOT bridge-related BRRTS cases at CTH P and CTH D.
pitch: Modest on their own, but a pattern worth a short piece: state highway bridge projects keep generating and then closing contamination cases in rural Marathon County. What's in the soil, and who pays to haul it?

name: Watch Ledger: roster shrinks even as 19 new cameras appear — and the new ones are private operators
what: Nineteen cameras added but the total fell from 2,117 to 2,111, with retailers listed as operators.
pitch: The new entries sampled are a Home Depot Rekor unit and an Axon camera run by a shopping center, not police. Private plate readers that police can query are a different accountability question than municipal ones.
